agent_notes: No source directly confirms 'Bhunwala' as one of the acquired 34 villages except a YouTube cycling-trip video title naming it as a waypoint between Netadwas and Dugoli (near Lunkaransar) — the single strongest lead. Census2011 mirror confirms Bhunwala is absent from the current Lunkaransar tehsil village list, and the merged administrative entry 'Mahajan Fieldfiring Range' shows population 2, consistent with an acquired/depopulated village, but no source names Bhunwala specifically within that merger. Rajasthan District Gazetteer (Bikaner, K.K. Sehgal, 1960s, archive.org full text) does NOT mention Bhunwala/Bhuwala at all — searched but found nothing, so not included as a source. Spelling variants Bhuwala, भूंवाला, भुवाला returned only unrelated results (mostly 'Bikanervala' snack-shop noise). Patrika (Rajasthan) has useful general '34 gaon' displacement coverage (2022 feature, 2019 incident report) but neither names Bhunwala. A 1987 Lok Sabha unstarred question on the Mahajan Field Firing Range (eLibrary Sansad) is a strong unexplored lead — the underlying PDF was not fetchable via WebFetch and needs manual retrieval to check for a village list.
